events.author: Solver
events.name: Tutorial: Attacks into Forests

options.text: Ranged units are much less effective against targets in woodland.

events.text: Your [unit] was ineffective in attacking the [rival] [unit] because the [unit] is in tree cover, which provides excellent protection against ranged attacks. Ranged units such as your [unit] firing into Scrub suffer a 25% penalty, and firing into Trees increases it to 50%.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Tutorial: City Defense
events.text: The enemy [unit] is in a city and very well protected. Units in cities will only take 1 HP damage from an attack until the city's own defenses are breached. Siege units such as Onager are especially effective against cities. A city tile always counts as Urban, so any bonuses against Urban terrain, such as Besieger, apply against cities. Since cities have potent defenses, especially when boosted by a defending unit, it is often wise to eliminate enemy units in the area before attempting to capture a city.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Tutorial: Defensive General

options.text: Generals can make a great difference.

events.text: Your attack against the [unit] was not very effective. The [unit] is led by a skilled General, [character], who has defensive abilities that are hard for your [unit] to overcome. Fighting against skilled generals is always going to be more difficult. It helps to assign General to your own units and to make use of promotions such as Heckler.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Tutorial: Defensive Terrain

options.text: Terrain can be a major defensive factor.

events.text: The enemy [unit] is in favorable Hill terrain that gives it a defense bonus. While Hill do not provide an inherent defense bonus, the [unit] has the Highlander promotion and therefore fights better in Hill. Your [unit] did not have enough strength to overcome this defensive bonus and did little damage. Try to avoid attacking units in terrain where they get defensive bonuses, or alternatively get enough offensive bonuses of your own.

events.text: The enemy [unit] is in Trees and has the Ranger promotion and therefore fights better in Trees. Your [unit] did not have enough strength to overcome this defensive bonus and did little damage. Try to avoid attacking units in terrain where they get defensive bonuses, or alternatively get enough offensive bonuses of your own.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Tutorial: Fortified Enemy

options.text: Fortified enemies will require an extra effort.

events.text: Your [unit] attacked a Fortify [unit], and the attack did little damage. When units Fortify, they can become very potent defenders that will take significant additional effort to kill. The Panic ability of War Elephant is an effective tool against Fortify enemies.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Tutorial: Home Defense

options.text: Some units fight better in their own territory.

events.text: Your [unit] attacked the [unit] but did not do much damage. The [unit] is in [rival] territory and receives a bonus when fighting in home territory. For example, Hunters units receive such a bonus from the Sentinel effect.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Tutorial: Long Distance Attacks

options.text: Ranged units do less damage at greater distances.

events.text: Your [unit] did little damage to the [unit] because of the Distance Modifier. The ability to attack at range is very powerful, but ranged units like your [unit] suffer a 20% penalty for each tile between it and the target. The powerful Eagle Eye promotion allows a unit to ignore the distance penalty.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Tutorial: Promoted Units

options.text: Highly promoted units are much more effective.

events.text: Even though your [unit] and the [rival] [unit] have similar base strength, your [unit] did not do much damage. The hostile [unit] has more Promotion that make it a stronger fighter overall. Promotion can make a huge difference in combat and therefore highly promoted units should be treated as very valuable assets - or especially dangerous targets!

events.author: Solver
events.name: Tutorial: River Crossing

options.text: Rivers pose a problem for the attacker.

events.text: Your [unit] attacked a hostile [unit] across a river and did little damage. Melee units receive a large attack penalty if attacking across a river, which makes rivers an effective natural defense. The Amphibious promotion can negate this penalty.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Tutorial: Urban Defense

options.text: Some units will be harder to beat in urban combat.

events.text: The [unit] is on Urban tile and has a bonus when defending Urban terrain. Because of that, your [unit] did not do much damage. If possible, you should engage in terrain the favors you. Some of your units may be able to get the Besieger promotion, which gives a bonus for attacking into Urban terrain.
